summary: The Lean theorem states that a finite lattice L with a least element is isomorphic to the full congruence lattice Con(A) of some algebra A on a nonempty finite carrier Fin n (finitely many finitary operations) if and only if there is a nonempty finite colored complete graph. Its coloring c : Fin n → Fin n → L must be symmetric, vanish exactly on the diagonal, satisfy the triangle inequality, be join-dense in L, and satisfy a path condition. The path condition says every pair whose color lies below the join of a nonempty seed set's colors is connected, by an equivalence-closure path, to images of seeds under label-decreasing self-maps. This is a faithful rendering of the characterization in Theorem 1.1(i). The main caveat is that the exact wording of the paper's Theorem 2.2 is not in the excerpt, and the decidability claims and parts (ii)–(iv) are not formalized.

coverage.why: The iff characterization appears faithful. The per-size decidability remark is not formalized but is trivial for a finite search.

Sketch check: necessity holds with c = principal congruence Cg, since unary polynomials are label-decreasing and Mal'cev chains give the path condition. Sufficiency holds with all label-decreasing maps as operations. So the Lean iff is a correct, standard criterion.

summary: The Lean theorem proves only that, for α ≥ 0 and a continuous bounded log-potential f, the bespoke EReal-valued variational value inf_q [α·P_f(q) + I(q)] is a finite real number. It is a finiteness/well-posedness lemma. The paper's main result (Theorem 2.3: the Ising perceptron pressure converges to this variational formula for bounded Borel f) is not formalized. The most important caveat is that the pattern functional is a bespoke limit along uniform discretizations, totalized via limUnder. Finiteness also follows almost directly from bounds such as I(q) ≥ 0 (take the zero field) and |P_f| ≤ K, so the statement says little about whether these definitions match the paper's.
